evidence.quote:
your view of Binghamville must be
like the old maps of Africa in the green geography, that said 'desert'
and 'interior' and 'savage tribes' from time to time
evidence.paraphrase: A character contrasts an outdated mental image of the town with how it has changed over time.

evidence.quote:
We've
moved on since you left us, you know.
evidence.paraphrase: A character notes that the community has changed since another left thirty years earlier.

evidence.quote:
"Maids? Maids? It used to be 'help,'" he had protested. "You don't mean
to say they have waitresses in Binghamville now?"
evidence.paraphrase: A returning character contrasts older terms and customs with present-day social arrangements in the town.

evidence.quote:
Something in the calm sun-bathed
picture tugged strongly at his heart. He thought suddenly of his mother
and his Aunt Delia
evidence.paraphrase: Varian is emotionally moved by the domestic scene, recalling his mother and aunt.

evidence.quote:
Lizzie says we were just on the edge of
the new age. It certainly is different. And of course I wouldn't go back
to it for anything.
evidence.paraphrase: A character contrasts the old-fashioned way of life with the changed present day.

evidence.quote:
But at her age mother was broken down and
old. She had to be. There were nine of us, and here there's only little
Dudley
evidence.paraphrase: A character contrasts her mother's worn-out state at a given age with her sister's youthful appearance now.

evidence.quote:
He winced. His associates were not accustomed to be so scrupulously
accurate. It seemed indecently long ago.
evidence.paraphrase: Varian reacts uncomfortably to the frank reminder of how much time has passed.

evidence.quote:
my mother
went to singing-school, and Lizzie was looking that up in a book, the
other day, to see what they did--she wanted it for a party!
evidence.paraphrase: A once-ordinary past custom has become a quaint curiosity researched for a party.
